chunks.text: Samuel Alipour-fard · THEORETiCAL PHYSiCiST · PH.D., MIT  (720) 413-7614 · |  samuel.alipourfard@yahoo.com · |  samcaf.github.io · |  samcaf · |  samuel-alipour-fard-0614a1367

Ph.D. In Theoretical Physics (Nuclear & Particle) at Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA (Aug. 2019 – May 2025). Thesis: Particles Inside Particles: The Flow of Energy in Quarks, Gluons, and Jets, advised by Jesse Thaler. Awarded a 2019 MIT Graduate Fellowship. Cumulative GPA: 4.0/4.0.

B.S. In Physics, College Of Creative Studies (Ccs) at University of California, Santa Barbara, Santa Barbara, CA (Sep. 2015 – Jun. 2019). Graduated with highest academic honors and with distinction in the major. Cumulative GPA: 4.0/4.0. Arnold Nordsieck Award (to a graduating senior of exceptional research promise); UCSB Regents Scholarship, all four years. Research advisor: Nathaniel Craig. Academic advisor: Tengiz Bibilashvili.

Graduate Researcher, Theoretical High‑Energy Physics (Advisor: Jesse Thaler) at Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA (Aug. 2019 – May 2025). Built the analytic and probabilistic foundations of energy‑correlator observables, and derived from scratch the mathematics underlying parton‑ shower simulation algorithms. Designed new energy correlators that make the low‑energy structure of high‑energy jets both analytically tractable and cheap to compute; introduced a continuous jet‑grooming method (PIRANHA).

Graduate Researcher, Theoretical High‑Energy Physics (Advisor: Jesse Thaler) at Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA (Aug. 2019 – May 2025). Designed new energy correlators that make the low‑energy structure of high‑energy jets both analytically tractable and cheap to compute; introduced a continuous jet‑grooming method (PIRANHA). Wrote and released the Monte‑Carlo and simulation software behind these results, and used it to test how the observables behave under de‑ tector noise and pileup contamination.

Graduate Researcher, Theoretical High‑Energy Physics (Advisor: Jesse Thaler) at Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA (Aug. 2019 – May 2025). Wrote and released the Monte‑Carlo and simulation software behind these results, and used it to test how the observables behave under de‑ tector noise and pileup contamination. Used the Energy Mover’s Distance, a metric on the space of radiation patterns, to reproduce standard collider observables from a geometric starting point.

Co‑Author, Superconducting‑Qubit Noise Study at Engineering Quantum Systems (EQuS) group, MIT (W. Oliver), Cambridge, MA (2024). Helped with Lindbladian‑dynamics simulations in Mathematica for a study of qubit‑state purity oscillations under anisotropic transverse noise; co‑author on the resulting Phys. Rev. A publication (see Publications).

Undergraduate Researcher, High‑Energy Physics (Advisor: Nathaniel Craig) at University of California, Santa Barbara, Santa Barbara, CA (Jan. 2017 – Jul. 2019). Adapted MadGraph, Pythia 8, and Delphes to simulate displaced decays and long‑lived particles (LLPs) in high‑energy collisions. Studied the reach of current and proposed colliders (LHC, CEPC, ILC, FCC‑ee, CLIC) for detecting LLPs; work published across three papers (see Publications) and presented in talks by N. Craig and S. Koren. Roig Summer Undergraduate Research Fellow (2018); Arnold Nordsieck Award (2019).

Undergraduate Researcher, Biophysics (Advisor: Greg Huber) at University of California, Santa Barbara, Santa Barbara, CA (Apr. 2016 – Jun. 2018). Modeled diffusion on “parking‑garage” (Terasaki‑ramp) topologies of the kind found in the rough endoplasmic reticulum, writing code to sim‑ ulate random walks on these surfaces.

Programming · Python (scientific computing, PyTorch/TensorFlow), C++, Mathematica, Bash, LATEX Methods · Monte‑Carlo methods and numerical simulation, statistical inference, analytic computation, Git Physics & Math · Quantum field theory and effective field theory, statistical mechanics, probability and information theory, perturbative QCD

Invited And Contributed Talks (2021 – 2024). Invited: ATLAS Jet Definitions subgroup, CERN (2021); LHCP (2022); “Jet Physics: From RHIC/LHC to EIC,” Stony Brook Center for Frontiers in Nuclear Science (2022). Contributed: Boost 2021 (remote), Boost 2022 (Hamburg), Boost 2024 (Genova).

MIT, Ph.D. Thesis Defense at Particles Inside Particles: The Flow of Energy in Quarks, Gluons, and Jets (2025). Public talk introducing the physics of quarks and gluons and my work on removing detector noise and contamination from particle data. Record‑ ing: youtu.be/ZI27iiX8qFM.

UC Santa Barbara, Undergraduate Research And Independent Seminars at Long‑lived particles; supersymmetric QM; generalized functions (2017 – 2018). Talks and posters on long‑lived particles at current and future colliders (UCSB Undergraduate Research Symposium, CCS RACA‑CON; recordings At Kitp). Organized and led interactive student seminars on supersymmetric quantum mechanics and on generalized functions.

Samuel Alipour‑Fard, Curriculum Vitae, 2, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA, Teaching Assistant, Department Of Physics at July 28, 2026 (Aug. 2020 – May 2025). TA for graduate courses in Quantum Field Theory (8.323), Effective Field Theory (8.851), Supersymmetric QFT (8.831), and General Relativity (8.962); and for undergraduate Electromagnetism (8.02), String Theory (8.251), and the Physics of Energy (8.21). Delivered one‑third of the lectures for the graduate SUSY QFT course during the instructor’s absence; designed problems, ran recitations, and helped put the EFT course on the MITx platform. Perfect TA evaluations in 8.251.

Learning Assistant, Learning Assistant Program at University of California, Santa Barbara, Santa Barbara, CA (Sep. 2017 – Jul. 2019). Supported upper‑division Quantum Mechanics, Classical Mechanics, and Thermodynamics & Statistical Mechanics, and lower‑division Electro‑ dynamics. This work contributed to N. Craig’s 2018 Cottrell Scholar Award.
Teaching Assistant, Calculus Iii at Boulder High School, Boulder, CO (Aug. 2014 – Jan. 2015). Helped high‑school students learn multivariable calculus, under teacher Akili Obeka.
2020 · Finalist, Paul and Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans · New York, NY

2017‑2019 Recipient, Regents Scholarship, Santa Barbara, CA.

Judge (2020 – 2025). Judged four editions of this international tournament for middle‑ and high‑school teams (Exeter NH, remote, Raleigh NC, Andover NH), with teams from the US, China, Georgia, and Tunisia.
Grader And Coaching Team (2022). Graded and discussed problems with the US coaching team for the 2022 USAPhO.

Founding Member & Application Reviewer at MIT graduate admissions, Cambridge, MA (2020 – 2022). Founding member of Graduates Advising Graduate Admissions; reworked application and essay prompts to broaden access. Reviewed appli‑ cations for the MIT Summer Research Program (MSRP).

Founder at Feynman Club, University of California, Santa Barbara, Santa Barbara, CA (2018). Ran a student club (with T. Bibilashvili) teaching quantum mechanics through the path‑integral approach, working problems together in a conversational style.

This is the engine behind PIRANHA , a continuous jet-grooming paradigm I introduced that smoothly removes contamination from jets instead of making hard, discrete cuts.
